segments.narration_text: You bring a careful recommendation into the room. The research is sound. The test plan has a measure and a stop condition. Someone asks about a competing priority. Engineering asks whose work will move. A person who was not in the meeting raises a concern afterward. The answer becomes, “Let's revisit this next quarter.” Chapter Fourteen opens with a version of that slow no.

segments.narration_text: Chapter Fifteen says an org chart is a start, but it will not show every decision path. Its first stakeholder lens is role type. A decision-maker can approve or stop the work. An influencer shapes that person's view. A gatekeeper controls access, capacity, or information. A champion advocates. A skeptic asks hard questions.

segments.narration_text: The book calls the pre-meeting work Shuttle Diplomacy. Learn the decision criteria before a deck hardens around one answer. Start with the person who will do the observation. Ask the operations lead what time the test would take and which staffing constraint would make it unsafe.
